agent-swarm.said: Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. # GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. - s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). - s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.

# Style override rule (Brett, Nov 7) — contract + enforcement

The rule:
1. Main apps — Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, Patches — SHARE one style/theme/design. Their override switch is OFF by default.
2. Every plugin and every UI asset has its own override switch, ON by default. On first install it stores its own copy seeded from the shared style, so everything looks the same until someone changes it.
3. A plugin/asset override changes ONLY that plugin/asset. It never changes the app it belongs to, other plugins, or the shared style.
4. Turning a plugin's override OFF makes it follow its app's (shared) style live.
5. Turning an app's override ON gives that app its own style; its plugins keep their own copies.

Do:

- Implement the resolution order in the shared theme/style engine (both web and Android twins where they exist): asset own copy (if override on) → app (if app override on) → shared main style.
- Switch in each app's and each plugin's settings (settings asset, no hard-coded UI). Migration: existing plugins get override ON with a copy of the current shared style; apps OFF.
- Write the rule to RULES.md and the brief template so every build follows it. CI check: every UI asset/plugin declares the override field.

- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' - A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). - Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.

- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
